prize_parts.citation: For the design of pH-responsive ionizable lipids and their controlled assembly into lipid nanoparticles that enable the delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B064) with Cullis, Hope and Madden. After round 1 I believe the case rests on a narrower and more defensible claim than I first stated. The decisive chemical step is the design principle that a lipid with a tuned pKa is near-neutral in circulation and cationic in the acidic endosome, where it drives a non-bilayer, fusogenic phase, together with the controlled assembly that traps nucleic acid at high efficiency. The Vancouver group reasoned this out from lipid polymorphism and demonstrated it first in antisense and then siRNA delivery, which is what made patisiran and, later, the mRNA vaccines possible. Later lipidoid screening and potency optimisation refined and extended the principle but did not originate it. No other shortlisted achievement so directly changed what clinicians can do, and the principle is validated across independent labs and approved products. The 2023 Medicine prize recognised the nucleoside-modified RNA cargo, not the carrier, so the delivery chemistry remains unrecognised.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weakest point. Any three-person cut leaves out MacLachlan on the Vancouver side and Anderson and Langer on the MIT side, and several colleagues (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke, Somfai, Zou) said the six-name record makes them unwilling to commit. I cannot settle priority from the supplied materials, so I hold my cut as a judgement. A second reservation is that some will read this as pharmaceutical formulation next to the 2023 Medicine prize. If the committee cannot agree on a defensible three names, B024 is the cleaner prize, and I would accept that outcome as scientifically sound even though my own ranking differs.

responses.point: He would move B064 up if it can be shown that Cullis, Hope and Madden hold the decisive step, the pKa-tuned lipid and rapid mixing, and he asks that the principle be separated from later formulation optimisation.
responses.response: This is the right test and I now state my case in those terms. The decisive step is the ionizable, pKa-tuned lipid with its pH-triggered non-bilayer fusogenic behaviour, plus the controlled-assembly route that gives high encapsulation. Those come from the Vancouver group, and the citation I propose is worded around that principle so that lipidoid libraries and later potency optimisation are not adjudicated. I accept that this rests on my recollection of dates, not verified records, and that the committee should check it against the expert report. If that check fails, I would not defend the trio.

responses.point: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics (B024) is a simple, general, cleanly attributed idea with four decades of consequences, and the attribution for PROTACs is easier to defend than for lipid nanoparticles.
responses.response: Johan's argument that B024 is a real conceptual step, and one with no credit problem, has moved me. I have not changed my first choice, because I weigh the change in what experimentalists and clinicians can do more heavily and I think a three-name delivery cut is defensible on the principle. But I have moved B024 into my alternatives in place of B012, since I could accept it as the committee's outcome. On PROTACs I agree attribution is somewhat cleaner than for lipids, yet the PROTAC and cereblon molecular-glue strands still call for different people, so I keep B046 as an alternative and not a first choice.

responses.point: The key insight is mechanistic, with the ionizable lipid promoting a non-bilayer fusogenic phase in the endosome, and the committee should state why the three-person line falls before Anderson and Langer.
responses.response: I agree and have built the mechanism into my citation and case. I would give the committee reason for the line this way: the concept (pKa-tuned ionizable lipid, fusogenic phase behaviour) and the first in vivo demonstration of the controlled-assembly route belong to Cullis, Hope and Madden, while the Anderson and Langer lipidoid libraries optimised potency within that framework. I hold this firmly enough to propose it, but I recognise that your trio with Anderson in place of Madden is the most defensible alternative and I am not certain the record rules it out.

responses.point: Sequencing by synthesis (B012) is chemistry at its core, with Balasubramanian and Klenerman as the unambiguous chemical pair, though B024 is the cleaner prize if attribution cannot be settled.
responses.response: Andrei's view that B012 reaches more fields than lipid delivery is fair, and I agree his Solexa pair is cleaner than my earlier three names including Rothberg. But the 1980 Sanger and Gilbert prize already honoured sequencing chemistry, and the competing claims from 454, Lynx and Columbia remain open, so the attribution problem is no easier than mine and the novelty argument is weaker. For that reason I have dropped B012 from my alternatives. I do agree with his fallback: if attribution cannot be settled, B024 is the sounder choice.

responses.point: He would need the expert report to establish priority in ionizable-lipid design before supporting a three-person list, and doubts that formulation should be the central chemical achievement so soon after the 2023 Medicine prize.
responses.response: I accept that without that priority evidence a three-person list is not safe, and I do not ask anyone to support it on my recollection alone. On the second point, the 2023 prize addressed the RNA cargo, the nucleoside modification that avoids innate immune activation, and a carrier that fuses with the endosome membrane is a different molecular problem solved with different chemistry. I would call the achievement lipid design, not formulation, because the pKa-tuned structure is the part that is molecularly specific.

uncertainties: Whether the record supports a cut after Cullis, Hope and Madden, or whether MacLachlan, Anderson or Langer should enter; I cannot verify priority and patent chronology from the supplied materials.
Whether a majority sees delivery lipid chemistry as core chemistry, not pharmaceutical formulation, after the 2023 Medicine prize.
Whether the committee will settle on B024 as the cleaner prize, given that no ballot reached five votes in round 1, and whether I should then accept it.
Whether B046 matures enough in clinical proof and credit allocation (PROTACs versus molecular glues) to become a full first choice.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure: I have no personal, institutional or collaborative connection to any shortlisted candidate, and my work on peptide-nanoparticle biosensors and hydrogels is thematically related to nanomaterials but not to the credited people. I note that my bioengineering and translational background may bias me toward discoveries with direct clinical reach, as Aqvist notes of his own preference for theory, and I have tried to weigh that against the cleaner attribution of B024. Emma Sparr's lipid self-assembly field overlaps with the subject, which she has disclosed; I do not consider it a recusal matter.
